lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans 413752 BOX OF VIDEO GAMES INCL NINTENDO ($100): photo shows a box of PS3/Xbox 360/Wii discs plus SNES Mario 3, not comparable. The PlayStation multi-lot entry: price shown inconsistently ($80 vs 7000 cents) and we have only one PS1 game, so irrelevant. GT64 PriceCharting entry: snippet only and the PAL GT64 page returned a list page with no price, so no verified figure. UNSOLD placeholder: not evidence. Moved PriceCharting guide figures to ASKING-type guides and added dated SOLD records for Bumper Bash, Maxi-15 and the Expansion Pak that the researcher missed. Researcher misidentified the Maxi-15 as an Atari multicart; it is an NES cart.
lots.guide_summary: Two ways to read it. As a Gowans box: close SOLD Gowans boxes of common loose Atari carts made $15 to $40 hammer (3 lots), but none had a scarce cart. Component view: SOLD eBay records (via PriceCharting) for Bumper Bash US$58 to US$100 (A$84 to A$143), Maxi-15 US$28 to US$53 (A$39 to A$76), Expansion Pak US$40 to US$50 (A$58 to A$72, if genuine), plus ASKING-type guides of about A$85 for the other seven games combined. Top of range A$375 is the optimistic sum of parts at the higher sold prices. No UNSOLD evidence. Rate 1 USD = 1.433 AUD.
lots.working: Keep: only the two label-confirmed scarce items use SOLD evidence. Lowest 24-month sales: Bumper Bash US$58.46 + Maxi-15 US$27.56 = US$86.02 x 1.433 = A$123.27; /1.198 = 102.9, round down to $100. The rest of the box (common carts, possible Expansion Pak) is upside. Flip: likely resale from SOLD medians, Bumper Bash about US$75 for a worn label (A$107) + Maxi-15 about US$50 (A$72) = A$179; less 13.4% eBay fees (A$24) and 2 outbound parcels at A$12 (A$24) = A$131; /2.396 = 54.7, round down to $55. Common carts at Gowans go for about $2 to $4 each, so they add little after fees. If the Expansion Pak is confirmed genuine and working, resale rises by about A$60 net, flip about $80.
lots.confidence_reason: Bumper Bash and Maxi-15 labels read in the photo and several dated SOLD records seen on PriceCharting pages I opened, but they are eBay (mostly US NTSC) sales via an aggregator, nothing is tested, the Bumper Bash label is worn, and the black item's identity is unconfirmed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Spectravideo Bumper Bash label read (1983 Spectravideo International, SA 218C, single player, paddle icon); title print faded and lower left of the label worn. Maxi-15 Pack label clean, 'assembled in Australia by Home Entertainment Suppliers', for the NES. Atari 32 in 1 is the 1988 Atari CX26163P. N64 carts PAL, labels good. Theme Park PS1 PAL in jewel case with a $15 shop sticker. Black item with gold-edge contacts and red end cap looks like an N64 Expansion Pak, label unreadable.
lots.condition: Loose, used, untested. Labels mostly fair to good; Bumper Bash label worn and faded. No boxes or manuals except the PS1 case.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the black item with the red end an official Nintendo 64 Expansion Pak (label should read NUS-007)? Is the Bumper Bash cart label intact apart from fading, and is the Theme Park disc present and unscratched? Has anything been tested?

lots.question_for_gowans: Roughly how many cards are in the bag, and how many are posted with Tasmanian stamps? Are there any real-photo cards of people, ships, mining towns or the West Coast, or any thylacine cards?

Ziegler-style open floral design, brick-red field with mild colour variation (abrash), cream main border with olive-brown vine, narrow guards.
